No change to the report or strategy was made in this part.

--- PART 2/6 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report / "Since we know the opponent set, we could design a strategy that adapts based on observed history." / "The parent already does something like this. We need to improve."
STRATEGY: The parent (slot7) is a TFT-with-forgiveness strategy that cooperates by default, retaliates after defections, and occasionally probes. The trace simulates the parent and other slots against the known opponent set, analyzing exploitable opponents (slot0, slot1, slot6, slot8) and the cost of probing. It proposes an adaptive strategy that starts with cooperation, probes with occasional defections, and increases defection if no retaliation occurs.

--- PART 3/6 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report / "So a safe adaptive strategy: - Start with C. - Keep a counter of our defections and opponent defections."
STRATEGY: The parent cooperates by default and only defects reactively or on a C,C,D pattern. The trace simulates probing/adaptive defection against opponent slots (AllC, slot6, slot8, slot5, etc.) and revises toward a safer adaptive strategy that starts with C and tracks defections.

--- PART 4/6 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Let's look at the parent's code again. Parent has a rule: if last6 all D, defect. If last6 all C, cooperate. Then TFT with forgiveness. It doesn't have a systematic probing schedule. It only defects when opponent defects. So it never probes against AllC. That's why it only gets 300 against slot0. If we add a probing mechanism that defects occasionally when opponent has been cooperating for a long time, we can exploit slot0 and maybe slot8."
STRATEGY: The parent cooperates on all-C history, defects on all-D history, then plays forgiving TFT, and never probes against an always-cooperating opponent. The trace simulates the parent and a proposed adaptive probing variant against slots 0–11, then changes the parent by adding a probe schedule: cooperate for the first 10 rounds, defect at round 11, and keep probing only if no retaliation is observed.

--- PART 5/6 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "So a strategy that cooperates for first 10 rounds, then probes every few rounds, and if it sees retaliation, stops probing for a long time, could work."
STRATEGY: The parent cooperates early, then probes with occasional defections, retaliates if the opponent defected last round, and stops probing after detecting retaliation. The trace simulates this against slots 0–11, computing probe/retaliation outcomes and scores. It changes the probe interval and punishment logic, ramping up to defecting every round only after repeated non-retaliation.

--- PART 6/6 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "So this strategy seems very solid. It exploits tolerant opponents and only takes minimal losses against strict ones. It should score significantly higher than the parent."
STRATEGY: Parent cooperates first, defects if opponent defected last round, otherwise probes by defecting while opponent cooperates. Simulated against slots 0–11 with probe intervals 3, 2, and 1. Changed to detect retaliation within 2 rounds, stop probing forever after retaliation, and shorten probe interval as successful probes accumulate.
